# Advanced Supermatter Handling
The Supermatter Crystal interacts strongly with the properties of its surrounding atmosphere.
Research indicates that certain atmospheric compositions can influence the behaviour and output characteristics of the crystal.
Nanotrasen research logs show promising results from controlled experimentation.
Advanced experimentation should only be performed by qualified senior Atmospheric Technicians and Engineering personnel.
Experiments exceeding established safety parameters must be conducted with appropriate authorization and risk assessment.
Unsafe experimentation may result in catastrophic consequences.
# NT-ESRD Experimental Archive
[color=orange]Nanotrasen Experimental Supermatter Research Division[/color]

## Experiment SM-T1
[color=cyan]Experiment Lead:[/color] NT-CE-TY-TY-TY
[color=cyan]Experiment Handler:[/color] NT-AT-LS
[color=cyan]Experiment Difficulty:[/color] Suitable for Junior Atmospheric Technicians with Chief Engineer supervision.
[color=cyan]Testing Facility:[/color] Pre-installed Nanotrasen Station [color=#000000]████████████[/color]
Station Classification: Standard issue Supermatter chamber.
[color=orange]Experiment Configuration[/color]
Chamber Size: Standard issue.
Chamber Atmosphere: Oxygen.
Coolant: Oxygen.
Installed Cooling: - Two sets of two Passive Vents. - Three radiator units per side.
Additional Cooling: - Freezer temperature set to 150 K. - Direct passive vent connection.
Electrical Disturbance Countermeasures: - Two grounding rods.
Safe Stress Emitter Limit: Two emitters.
Experimental Stress Limit: Six emitters.
[color=orange]Automation Recommendations[/color]
Air Alarm automation is strongly advised.
Scrubber configuration: Remove all gases except Oxygen.
[color=orange]Project Summary[/color]
Experiment demonstrated stable operation with profitable power harvesting potential.
Moderate radiation output was recorded.
Recommended harvesting configuration: - Four emitters. - Six NT Radiation Collectors.
Alternative coolant gases may be considered. Nitrogen coolant substitution showed comparable stability.

## Project SM-Zero
[color=cyan]Experiment Lead:[/color] NT-CE-LS
[color=cyan]Experiment Handler:[/color] NT-CE-LS
[color=cyan]Experiment Difficulty:[/color] Senior Atmospheric Technician clearance.
[color=cyan]Recommended Facilities:[/color]
Pre-existing Nanotrasen facilities:
- Facility designation [color=#000000]████████[/color] - Facility designation [color=#000000]████████[/color]
Both facilities contained legacy or modified Supermatter chamber layouts.
[color=orange]Experiment Configuration[/color]
Chamber Temperature: Below 70 K.
Pressure Supply: Oxygen — 200 kPa.
Experimental Atmosphere: Primarily Oxygen with approximately one tenth Nitrogen.
Coolant: - Oxygen. - Tritium. - Nitrogen.
Overpressure Countermeasures: - Inlet Valve configured at 300 kPa. - Signal valve controlled by operational procedure.
Cooling System: Three parallel radiator branches.
Six radiators installed per branch.
Additional Cooling: Three freezers connected directly through passive vent systems.
[color=orange]Automation Recommendations[/color]
Required automation: - Pressure floor monitoring. - Temperature-sensitive emitter activation.
[color=orange]Experiment Results[/color]
Safe emitter limit: Six emitters.
Estimated safe emitter limit: Sixteen emitters.
Emitters used during testing: Thirty-two emitters.
[color=red]CRITICAL EVENT:[/color]
Geiger monitoring equipment reached maximum measurement capacity.
Immediate increase of radiation shielding was required.
Emitter activation should be separated into multiple stages to prevent rapid stress escalation.
Maximum recorded output: 11.3 MW.
Experiment demonstrated exceptional profitability with significant operational risk.
Further experiments require consultation with affected departments.
